entryPoints.invariant: A primary session may not arm supervision or run a guarded tool without the pre-tool checkpoint.
A backlog close marker is replayed only when its recorded identity, data directory, and task id still agree.
entryPoints.note: Called from the staging and replay owners inside its own library; bin/fm-teardown.sh is the executable that reaches both.

entryPoints.invariant: An investigation or review may not complete while a captain call it raised is still open.
A primary session may not leave its declared working directory through an unchecked shell command.

rejectedCallSites.reason: Names the hook owner in a // header comment; the policy module is imported by it rather than calling it.

entryPoints.invariant: The watcher executes a custom state check only against the exact bytes an intentional registration bound.
A retired custom state check loses its content binding through the owner path, never a hand-composed remove.
entryPoints.reason: No script calls it: bin/fm-teardown.sh removes a spawned task's check artifacts on its own path, so this is the retirement command firstmate runs for a check it registered by hand.

entryPoints.invariant: A no-mistakes ship task's PR head carries the obligated commit identity and no contaminated commit.
A cursor launcher alias is accepted only with evidence that the executable really is cursor-agent.
entryPoints.note: The resolver that every cursor spawn traverses calls it before accepting a candidate.

entryPoints.invariant: Every maintained prose surface is classified exactly once and its local links resolve.
Every enforce-style entry point in bin/ declares a call site that still names it in executable text, rather than shipping with no declared caller at all.
A no-mistakes gate agent may not drive fleet lifecycle commands.
A fleet mutation that runs without the verified per-home lock or from a tangled checkout is announced to the operator.
entryPoints.reason: An advisory reporter, not a refusal: bin/fm-guard.sh always exits 0 (its only top-level exits are the two `exit 0` statements), so no invocation can act on a failing status and a fleet mutation from a tangled checkout prints the banner and then proceeds. The lock-and-tangle invariant in its previous declaration has no blocking owner at this call site; see docs/verification/enforcing-call-sites.md.

entryPoints.invariant: Only the actor holding a task's supervision lease may change that task.
A supervision lease taken for a guarded change is released on every exit path.
Tracked GitHub workflows lint clean against the pinned actionlint.

rejectedCallSites.reason: Names the workflow linter in a # comment describing the lint step; bin/fm-lint.sh is the command the step runs.

entryPoints.invariant: The tracked shell surface lints clean against one pinned ShellCheck, identically in CI and the pre-push gate.
The required no-mistakes status workflow acts only on validated input.
Every tracked outbound write records its exact payload bytes, digest, and provider verdict in the ledger.
entryPoints.note: Known-good reference: the shared enforcement owner landed by PR 47 (merge 0a519ea).

entryPoints.invariant: A task's recorded PR identity is validated before a merge poll is armed for it.

rejectedCallSites.reason: Names the script inside a printf of operator next-step text, not in a command.
Names the script inside the quoted heredoc that renders the branch agent's tool list.

entryPoints.invariant: A remote job runs only with complete, well-formed transport settings.
entryPoints.note: Called by the job entry path inside its own library, which bin/fm-on.sh and the remote handoff owners traverse.

entryPoints.invariant: Curated durable memory is injected at session start only while the home is within its startup-memory budget.
entryPoints.note: Known-good reference: the gate wired to its startup consumer by PR 46 (merge 0e826aa).

entryPoints.invariant: A subagent may not reach the primary's guarded tool surface unchecked.
The complete-regression lane partition stays proven and every portable serial shard stays inside its job-cap budget.
A launcher or observation shell resolves the qualified tool profile before work depends on it.
A primary turn may not end blind while fleet work is under way.
The same turn-end guard reaches a Cursor primary through its own stop-hook owner.

rejectedCallSites.reason: Names the stop-hook owner inside a printf of supervision instruction text, not in a command.

entryPoints.invariant: The same turn-end guard reaches a Grok primary through its registered hook.
A pre-collapse decision identity still verifies against the surviving captain-hold owner.
entryPoints.reason: One-release compatibility shim for briefs written before the decision collapse; the surviving owner bin/fm-captain-hold.sh:verify carries the production call site, and this surface is invoked only by an in-flight brief.

entryPoints.invariant: The secondmate registry stays parseable, with absolute, unique, non-overlapping homes.
entryPoints.reason: A standalone re-check surface for an operator; the same validate_registry predicate already runs inside the transactional seed path, so the invariant is enforced at the write boundary rather than here.

entryPoints.invariant: Activation staging is refused when an isolation input is missing.
entryPoints.reason: An opt-in strictness flag on a captain-authorized launcher cutover procedure that no script schedules; the procedure itself is the invoker.

entryPoints.invariant: Watched tooling with an available or inert update is reported to the supervisor.
entryPoints.reason: A reporter, not an enforcement point: it prints a wake line and refuses nothing. Discovered only because its name carries the word check.

entryPoints.invariant: A cmux operation that the daemon denied is refused with the owner action rather than retried blind.
entryPoints.note: Called from the adapter's own send and capture paths, which every cmux-backed lifecycle command traverses.

entryPoints.invariant: A cmux operation without daemon authorization is refused rather than treated as a transport error.
entryPoints.note: Called from the adapter's own send and capture paths, which every cmux-backed lifecycle command traverses.

entryPoints.invariant: Away mode is re-entered only when any surviving launch record is still well formed and its return catch-up has cleared.
entryPoints.note: Called on both re-entry paths inside the launcher, which is the only writer of the away-mode record.

entryPoints.invariant: Ordinary captain work is refused while away mode is active or return catch-up is still pending.
A session backend is used only when an implemented adapter answers to that exact name.
A task is spawned only on a backend whose adapter implements task spawning.
A task's recorded endpoint is proven to belong to that task before any command acts on the session it names.
The watcher-down banner is announced in full once per down episode and as a reminder afterwards.
entryPoints.reason: Presentation bookkeeping, not a refusal: it decides how loudly the existing alarm prints and never changes whether a fleet mutation is allowed. Discovered only because bin/fm-guard.sh namespaces its helpers fm_guard_*.

entryPoints.invariant: A recovered watcher clears the announced-episode marker so the next down episode announces in full.
entryPoints.reason: Presentation bookkeeping, not a refusal: it removes a marker file and never changes whether a fleet mutation is allowed. Discovered only because bin/fm-guard.sh namespaces its helpers fm_guard_*.

entryPoints.invariant: A read-only guard pass reports whether this down episode was already announced without claiming it.
entryPoints.reason: A read-only predicate over the banner marker, not a refusal. Discovered only because bin/fm-guard.sh namespaces its helpers fm_guard_*.

entryPoints.invariant: One continuous watcher-down episode keys on the failing condition rather than the beacon mtime.
entryPoints.reason: A pure key formatter for the banner marker, not a refusal. Discovered only because bin/fm-guard.sh namespaces its helpers fm_guard_*.

entryPoints.invariant: A lab operation never touches the shared default Herdr session.
entryPoints.note: Called by every mutating lab subcommand inside its own script, which is the only owner of lab sessions.

entryPoints.invariant: A lab session is addressed only by a well-formed fm-lab-* name this script could have created.
entryPoints.note: Called by every lab subcommand inside its own script before the name reaches the backend.

entryPoints.invariant: A lab session is destroyed only after its tripwire proves the session is the one this script created.
entryPoints.note: Called by the lab teardown paths inside its own script, immediately before the destructive call.

entryPoints.invariant: Follow-on work behind a registered public loop is held until that loop's reply has landed.
A secondmate home's data, state, config and projects directories resolve inside that home and nowhere else.
entryPoints.note: Called by validate_secondmate_home in its own library, which bin/fm-bootstrap.sh, bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh, bin/fm-stow-cascade.sh and bin/fm-config-push.sh traverse.

entryPoints.invariant: A secondmate home is accepted only when it resolves to a real directory that is not the active firstmate home and whose marker names the expected id.
The secondmate registry parses with unique, non-overlapping host, root and home bindings, and any expected id and home still agree with it.
A status presentation helper runs only after bin/fm-classify-lib.sh has been sourced.
entryPoints.reason: A lazy module loader, not a refusal: `require` here means import, and the function sources bin/fm-classify-lib.sh on demand rather than rejecting any input. One caller (bin/fm-wake-lib.sh's count helper) degrades to a zero count when the load fails instead of refusing, which is the opposite of a gate.
